transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Ross (Redwood SE), Rebecca Liu (Acme - Head of ML), Mark Thompson (Acme - Platform Eng), Diane Okafor (Acme - Security), Carlos Vega (Acme - PM)

Summary:
Quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed on three benchmark workloads, go/no-go thresholds for latency/quality/stability, reporting format (CSV + Grafana + summary PDF), and a 2-week POC timeline with a 2-day benchmark window. Action items and SOW delivery dates agreed.

Topics:
- Success criteria: latency, quality/accuracy, stability/error rate
- Workload sizing: representative queries, concurrency, token lengths
- Benchmarks: warm/cold cache, KV cache behavior, throughput targets
- Timelines: SOW, dataset delivery, benchmark window, sign-off
- Reporting: raw logs CSV, Grafana dashboard link, executive summary PDF

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll run for about 50 minutes, big agenda is to lock down success criteria and the acceptance tests for the POC, make sure we're aligned on what go / no-go looks like.
[00:18] Rebecca: Great, thanks Jamie. We brought Mark and Diane and Carlos, want to make sure security and platform constraints are accounted for.
[00:27] Evan: I'll cover the benchmark plan and what's measurable. Quick note, transcription might mangle some tech names, sorry in advance.
[00:35] Mark: Cool, we have a few constraints: VPC peering for the private test, and we need low network egress during benchmark windows. Also our traffic shape is spiky - some minutes at 80 rps, others near 5.
[00:48] Diane: From security we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration details, and audit log formats. Also, no model artifacts should be left on shared storage post-POC.
[01:03] Jamie: Understood. Let's start with success criteria. We propose three primary axes: latency, quality, stability. For latency we recommend P95 < 300ms for generative requests at our target token length (avg 128 tokens) - is that reasonable?
[01:18] Rebecca: 300ms P95 sounds ambitious but in line with our SLAs; can we define cold vs warm cache numbers? Our users expect consistent latency, cold starts must be documented.
[01:30] Evan: Yeah we'll run both warm and cold tests. Proposal: cold-start P95 < 700ms, warm P95 < 300ms. We'll run warm tests after priming KV cache with a representative prefix set.
[01:44] Carlos: Also need throughput criteria — we think baseline is sustained 50 rps with bursts to 80 rps without degradation.
[01:50] Jamie: So put throughput as 95% of requests at target concurrency sustain under the latency threshold, and no request queueing beyond a 500ms additional wait.
[02:03] Rebecca: For quality, we want automated metrics plus human review. What's Redwood's approach?
[02:08] Evan: We'll run a sample of 5k queries across three workloads: short Q&A, long-form generation (avg 512 tokens), and instruction-following. Automated metrics: ROUGE/BLEU are limited for these tasks, so plan is to do a human eval on a 200-sample subset and use model-specific heuristics for the rest (e.g., semantic similarity via embeddings). Pass threshold: >= 85% acceptable in human eval for primary workload.
[02:30] Mark: That 85% human acceptability is ... okay. We also need a regression guard: model should not hallucinate on P0 flows; any P0 hallucination is immediate fail.
[02:40] Diane: Define P0 flows?
[02:42] Rebecca: P0 = authentication and billing responses where factual accuracy is required.
[02:47] Evan: We'll add a targeted test set for P0 flows — zero hallucinations tolerated.
[02:51] Jamie: Stability wise, error rate must be <1% (5xx / timeouts) during benchmark window, and no sustained memory leaks or crashes across a 24-hour soak if we run extended tests. For go/no-go: all three axes must meet thresholds, but we allow one minor fail on a non-blocking metric to be remediated in a follow-up sprint within agreed window.
[03:12] Carlos: How will you present results? We need raw logs for our infra team and an executive summary for leadership.
[03:18] Evan: We'll provide: 1) CSV export with per-request latency, tokens, model variant, error codes; 2) Grafana dashboard link with P50/P95/P99, throughput, error rates; 3) PDF exec summary with pass/fail for each success criteria and recommended optimizations.
[03:33] Rebecca: Ensure timestamps are in UTC and include request IDs so we can correlate.
[03:37] Evan: Absolutely. Also we'll include KV cache hit/miss tags so you can see warm vs cold behavior.
[03:44] Jamie: Timeline — we recommend: SOW out in 3 days, Acme provides dataset in 4 days, Redwood prepares harness in 6 days, run the 2-day benchmark during week of 2025-09-22, then 3 business days to deliver report. So sign-off should happen by end of first week of October if all goes well.
[04:01] Rebecca: Sounds fine. One question on model variants — can we test a quantized variant to check cost/latency tradeoffs?
[04:08] Evan: Yes, we'll include a baseline full-precision model and a 4-bit quantized variant. We'll measure cost per 1M tokens and latency delta. Acceptance criteria apply to the baseline; quantized can be evaluated as optimization — but if quantized fails baseline, we still consider baseline results for go/no-go.
[04:25] Mark: For network setup, we'll need instructions to spin up a test VPC and a temporary route for Redwood endpoints; Diane will coordinate security.
[04:33] Diane: We'll need to review the data retention policy — logs retained only for 30 days and then rotated, and review how keys are stored.
[04:40] Jamie: We'll send a short security packet (SOC2 summary, KMS integration notes, audit log schema).
[04:46] Carlos: Ok, acceptance tests — let's be explicit:
[04:49] Jamie: Test 1 — Latency: Warm P95 <= 300ms for primary workload (avg 128 tokens); Cold P95 <= 700ms. Test 2 — Quality: Human eval >= 85% acceptable on 200-sample subset; zero hallucinations on P0 test set. Test 3 — Stability: Error rate <1% during benchmark window; no crashes/memory leaks in 24h soak. Passing all three = GO. If one non-P0 metric fails by <10% we can qualify for remediation.
[05:20] Rebecca: Agree. Also, reporting format: CSV for raw logs (request_id, timestamp, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, variant, error_code), Grafana link, and a 2-page exec summary PDF.
[05:33] Evan: We'll also include a small sample of transcripts for human eval and a Trello/Notion board with action items.
[05:40] Mark: For workload sizing: use 5k total queries broken across three workloads — 2k short Q&A, 2k long-form, 1k instruction-following. Concurrency patterns: sustained 50 rps with two 1-hour burst windows at 80 rps.
[05:55] Rebecca: That distribution matches our traffic. For the human eval rubric, can Redwood provide the template?
[05:59] Evan: Yes, we'll share a rubric with binary accept/reject plus a short comment field.
[06:05] Carlos: Any legal/contract blockers?
[06:07] Jamie: SOW will be standard with a POC clause; no charge for baseline benchmarking but if extended infra required we may bill for dedicated capacity during the run — we'll call that out in the SOW.
[06:20] Diane: Can we get a data processing addendum for the sample dataset?
[06:23] Jamie: Yes we'll attach a DPA to the SOW.
[06:27] Rebecca: Excellent. Anything else?
[06:30] Evan: One more technical note — we'll instrument KV cache metrics and provide warmup scripts; please flag any request prefixes you want excluded.
[06:38] Mark: We'll provide a list of P0 prefixes and sensitive queries.
[06:42] Jamie: Ok let's recap next steps and owners: SOW from Jamie, dataset from Rebecca, harness from Evan, network contact from Diane, benchmark scheduling from Carlos. We'll aim to have the benchmark week of 2025-09-22.
[06:58] Rebecca: Sounds good, looking forward to the SOW.
[07:00] Jamie: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with the SOW and security packet.
